programs.name: wpcuncompress
programs.purpose: Decompress a two-dimensional wavelet-packet-compressed array into binary floats.
programs.float_sensitive_notes: The compressed representation is explicitly documented as platform-dependent. The wavelet decoder's floating-point operations also affect exact output. wpcRead, wpcN1, wpcN2 and wpcUncompress belong to the separate WPC library.
programs.difficulty_reason: The main program is short, but reproducing its wavelet-packet decompressor and platform-dependent compressed format requires substantial codec work.

test_cases.description: Compress and decompress a small spike section.
test_cases.command: suspike nt=64 ntr=8 k1=20 k2=4 | sustrip | wpccompress n1=64 n2=8 error=0.01 | wpcuncompress > out.bin

test_cases.description: Exercise a different compression error and input shape.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=128 ntr=16 | sustrip | wpccompress n1=128 n2=16 error=0.05 | wpcuncompress > out.bin

programs.name: percent
programs.purpose: Print 100 times the ratio of two positional numeric arguments.
programs.float_sensitive_notes: Uses double arithmetic and platform-dependent atof and %g formatting; missing positional arguments cause undefined behavior. A zero denominator produces zero.
programs.difficulty_reason: It parses two positional arguments and performs one double-precision calculation.
programs.license_note: No copyright or license notice appears in the file.

programs.name: sutetraray
programs.purpose: Trace three-dimensional rays through a tetrahedral model and produce surface travel-time tables.

params.name: nxgd
params.description: Number of x grid samples; rounded up to an odd number by (nxgd/2)*2+1.

params.name: nygd
params.description: Number of y grid samples; rounded up to an odd number by (nygd/2)*2+1.

params.name: shootupward
params.description: Initial ray direction; 1 is upward and -1 downward.

params.name: tmax
params.description: Maximum tracing time used to compute the default ntwf.

params.name: ntwf
params.description: Maximum wavefront count; subsequently increased to at least ifwf2dump+nwf2dump.

params.name: edgemax
params.description: Maximum triangle edge length before splitting, in grid-spacing units.

params.name: fsx
params.description: First source x coordinate; subsequently snapped to the grid and shifted by 0.01*dxgd.

params.name: dsx
params.description: Source x spacing; subsequently quantized to at least one grid interval.

params.name: fsy
params.description: First source y coordinate; subsequently snapped to the grid and shifted by 0.01*dygd.

params.name: dsy
params.description: Source y spacing; subsequently quantized to at least one grid interval.

params.name: irefseq
params.description: Reflector sequence; absent means an empty sequence.

params.name: crfile
params.description: Optional binary cosine and ray-distance output file.

params.name: ifwf2dump
params.description: First wavefront to dump; parsed and initialized only when wffile is open.

params.name: nwf2dump
params.description: Number of wavefronts to dump; parsed and initialized only when wffile is open.

params.name: jpfile
params.description: Diagnostic output file; failure to open falls back to stderr.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Wavefront construction, interpolation, geometric predicates and polynomial solvers use floating-point arithmetic and transcendental functions; branch decisions are sensitive to rounding. ifwf2dump and nwf2dump are uninitialized when wffile is absent but are subsequently read. area3d and tetra_volume are calls to the separate tetra library.
programs.difficulty_reason: The program implements extensive three-dimensional wavefront construction, ray tracing, reflection and interpolation.

test_cases.description: Trace a small constant-velocity model with wavefront output enabled.
test_cases.command: tetramod nxhz=3 nyhz=3 nhz=1 hzfile=hz.bin > model.txt && sutetraray nxgd=5 nygd=5 nxt=3 nyt=3 ntakeoff=3 nazimuth=8 ntwf=30 wffile=wf.bin ifwf2dump=2 nwf2dump=1 < model.txt > tt.su

test_cases.description: Trace downward with alternate sampling and auxiliary output.
test_cases.command: tetramod nxhz=3 nyhz=3 nhz=1 hzfile=hz.bin > model.txt && sutetraray nxgd=5 nygd=5 nxt=3 nyt=3 shootupward=-1 takeoff=20 ntakeoff=3 nazimuth=8 ntwf=30 wffile=wf.bin ifwf2dump=2 nwf2dump=1 rayfile=rays.bin < model.txt > tt.su

programs.name: tetramod
programs.purpose: Build a three-dimensional tetrahedral velocity model and a horizon visualization file.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: TETRAMOD - TETRAhedron MODel builder. In each layer, velocity gradient

params.name: nxhz
params.description: Number of x samples per horizon.

params.name: nyhz
params.description: Number of y samples per horizon.

params.name: nhz
params.description: Number of horizons excluding the model base.

params.name: ficth
params.description: Fictitious horizon indices; absent means none, and a single -1 also means none.

params.name: zmax
params.description: Initial maximum depth; model construction updates it using horizon depths.

params.name: x{ihz}file
params.description: Per-horizon binary x-coordinate grid; absent uses a uniform grid. ihz ranges from 0 to nhz-1.

params.name: y{ihz}file
params.description: Per-horizon binary y-coordinate grid; absent uses a uniform grid.

params.name: z{ihz}file
params.description: Per-horizon binary depth adjustment grid; absent uses zero.

params.name: v{ihz}file
params.description: Per-horizon binary velocity adjustment grid; absent uses zero.

params.name: dvdz{ihz}file
params.description: Per-horizon binary velocity-gradient adjustment grid; absent uses zero.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Geometry construction uses interpolation, iterative conjugate-gradient and Gaussian elimination routines, square roots and floating-point comparisons. Supplying fewer corner-array elements than nhz leaves remaining allocated values uninitialized. The horizon file uses native binary integers and floats. area3d and tetra_volume are calls to the separate tetra library.
programs.difficulty_reason: It constructs a three-dimensional mesh with numerical solvers, complex connectivity and several binary grid inputs.

test_cases.command: tetramod nxhz=3 nyhz=3 nhz=1 hzfile=hz.bin > model.txt

test_cases.description: Build two layers with explicit depths, velocities and gradients.

programs.name: spsplot
programs.purpose: Draw a triangulated sloth model as a shaded PostScript plot.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SPSPLOT - plot a triangulated sloth function s(x,z) via PostScript

params.name: style
params.description: Plot orientation; normal selects normal style, all other values select seismic.

params.name: labelsize
params.description: Axis label size; the selfdoc incorrectly says 12.

params.name: dxnum
params.description: Numbered x tick interval; zero selects automatic ticks.

params.name: gridx
params.description: X grid style: none, dot, dash or solid.

params.name: dznum
params.description: Numbered z tick interval; zero selects automatic ticks.

params.name: gridz
params.description: Z grid style: none, dot, dash or solid.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Shading and plotting use floating-point scaling, trigonometry and formatted PostScript output. The source notes optimization-dependent errors under NEXTSTEP 3.1. readModel belongs to the triangle library and the PostScript drawing primitives belong to the PostScript library.
programs.difficulty_reason: It traverses a triangulated model and generates shaded PostScript with axis and style options.

test_cases.command: trimodel xmin=0 xmax=1 zmin=0 zmax=1 sfill=0.5,0.5,0,0,1,0.1,0.2 | spsplot title=Model > model.ps

test_cases.description: Exercise alternate orientation, grids and line widths.
test_cases.command: trimodel xmin=0 xmax=1 zmin=0 zmax=1 sfill=0.5,0.5,0,0,1,0.1,0.2 | spsplot style=normal gridx=dash gridz=dot gedge=0.2 gtri=0.7 axeswidth=2 ticwidth=1 gridwidth=0.5 > model.ps

programs.name: gbbeam
programs.purpose: Make Gaussian-beam synthetic seismograms from ray endpoints and a receiver surface.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: GBBEAM - Gaussian beam synthetic seismograms for a sloth model

params.name: xg
params.description: Receiver-surface x coordinates; must have the same count as zg.

params.name: zg
params.description: Receiver-surface z coordinates; must have the same count as xg.

params.name: ng
params.description: Number of receivers uniformly spaced along the surface.

params.name: ang
params.description: Angles in degrees corresponding to amp; must be nondecreasing and match its count.

params.name: nt
params.description: Number of output samples per receiver.

params.name: reftrans
params.description: Enable complex reflection and transmission coefficients.

params.name: prim
params.description: Ray reflection-count selection; 0 selects direct and 1 single-reflected rays.

params.name: aperture
params.description: Receiver aperture parameter; if supplied the code applies asin(aperture*PI/180).

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Cubic interpolation, complex Gaussian-beam calculations, attenuation, transcendental functions, FFTs and accumulation order affect exact results. Input RayEnd records use native binary structure layout. The supplied aperture is transformed with asin rather than a simple degree-to-radian conversion.
programs.difficulty_reason: It combines dynamic ray endpoints, spline interpolation, complex Gaussian beams, attenuation and FFT synthesis.

test_cases.description: Generate ray endpoints and a small receiver section.
test_cases.command: trimodel xmin=0 xmax=1 zmin=0 zmax=1 sfill=0.5,0.5,0,0,1,0,0 | triray nangle=11 fangle=-30 langle=30 > rays.bin && gbbeam xg=0,1 zg=1,1 ng=8 nt=128 dt=0.004 < rays.bin > syn.bin

test_cases.description: Exercise attenuation, source amplitudes and beam width.
test_cases.command: trimodel xmin=0 xmax=1 zmin=0 zmax=1 sfill=0.5,0.5,0,0,1,0,0 | triray nangle=11 fangle=-30 langle=30 > rays.bin && gbbeam xg=0,1 zg=1,1 ng=8 nt=128 dt=0.004 atten=1 bw=0.1 ang=-30,30 amp=0.5,1 fpeak=20 < rays.bin > syn.bin
